chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who performs an Umrat al-Mufradah, and he performs the Tawaf of the House as the obligatory Tawaf, then he has intercourse with his wife before he performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has spoiled his Umrah, and upon him is a camel (as expiation), and he stays in Makkah free from Ihram until the month in which he performed Umrah passes, then he goes out to the time which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated for the people of his country, so he enters Ihram from it and performs Umrah.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةُ: As-Safa and Al-Marwa (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Umrat al-Mufradah (Umrah performed independently, not combined with Hajj)
key_terms.مُحِلًّا: Free from Ihram / in a state of Ihram (contextual)
key_terms.يَغْشَى أَهْلَهُ: He has intercourse with his wife

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation and procedure for a man who has intercourse with his wife before Sa'i during Umrat al-Mufradah?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sexual intercourse during Umrat al-Mufradah before Sa'i invalidates the pilgrimage, requiring a camel (*badana*) as expiation. The pilgrim must remain in Makkah until the lunar month of his Umrah concludes, then exit in a state of Ihram to perform a fresh Umrah from the Miqat, illustrating the distinct legal consequences of timing violations in Shia jurisprudence. This highlights the rigorous preservation of ritual order (*tartib*) emphasized by the Ahl al-Bayt.
